external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who uses the dispatch console from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network. They open the dispatch console in their browser.
external_entities.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work through a SOAP feed.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript application opened by duty engineers in their browser.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer; it runs in the production control plane.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
processes.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: A process on the corporate network that pulls, parses, archives, and posts planned work.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: It presents an API token. That token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: A database containing job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order in it carries the token or the session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token. How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder where the importer writes each downloaded scheduling document.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_stores.name: corporate file store
data_stores.description: The corporate file store containing the schedule archive folder.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: serve console
data_flows.description: The corporate web host serves the dispatch console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API cross-origin.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The console and the API are served from different origins, so the API answers the console cross-origin. Whoever configured CORS did not record which origins the API allows, or whether it allows credentials.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether that socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after it is open.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating tokens or sessions

data_flows.name: pull planned work
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the scheduling partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies our importer, or how our importer identifies the partner.

data_flows.name: write schedule archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded XML document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_flows.data_description: downloaded XML document containing planned work

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: It presents an API token. That token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers and the schedule importer are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: A same-company zone holding the live estate and authority to move crews and change depot work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The control plane is the same company and the same staff, but it is the zone that holds the live estate
trust_boundaries.notes: A corporate laptop holds none of those rights. The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: A zone controlled by the separate company that provides the scheduling feed.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database's contents are confidential.
assumptions.basis: It holds crew mobile numbers, which are personal data, and tokens or sessions that created job orders.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API is internal rather than internet-facing.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the production control plane where the API runs is not reachable from the internet.
